subject.title: Feature request: Escalating stall recovery for sub-agents (nudge → kill)

question: Should OpenClaw add subagent-specific inactivity recovery as nudge-then-kill, keep the newer diagnostic active-abort path as the supported recovery, or split this across the broader session activity/watchdog work?
rationale: The problem is real and high impact, but the remaining behavior changes default runtime policy, config shape, forced-abort semantics, and what users see in chat channels.

options.title: Keep This As Canonical Design
options.body: Use this issue to decide the supported automatic subagent stall policy before implementation, reusing current diagnostic and subagent-control seams.

options.title: Treat Diagnostics As Sufficient
options.body: Close or narrow this issue only if maintainers explicitly decide diagnostic active-abort is the product answer and no nudge/channel-visible policy is wanted.

options.title: Defer To Activity Watchdog
options.body: Make the automatic policy depend on the broader session activity/watchdog issues and keep this issue linked as the subagent-specific requirement.

recommendation.title: Keep This As Canonical Design
recommendation.body: Use this issue to decide the supported automatic subagent stall policy before implementation, reusing current diagnostic and subagent-control seams.

likelyOwner.reason: Current blame and recent PR ownership put the central subagent runtime/control/config seams closest to vincentkoc.
